defect.summary: gate4-sunset's leg B cannot tell an EMPTY successor reference from a real one, and said nothing about it. Measured 2026-10-03 with leg B actually reading: a successor paper whose value is "", "   ", a tab-and-newline, or a real brief name produces FOUR INDISTINGUISHABLE SILENT readings, no blind code between them. Codex's FAIL is correct. T21's ceiling line predicted exactly this limit - 'this leg reads that the successor paper was WRITTEN, never that the successor is ADEQUATE' - and the gate shipped printing the prediction instead of acting on it, which is this campaign's own named defect: a disclosure instead of a fix.
defect.ground: ⛔ AND IT IS NOT FIXABLE IN THE READER, WHICH IS WHY THIS TICKET IS A CEILING LINE AND NOT A CHECK. At bytes, 2026-10-03: src/mica/log.ts:101 - MicaLogRecord is EXACTLY (sequenceNumber, timestamp, moduleId, eventType, outcome) plus an optional actionId, with NO payload field, and the bridge's own kinds-census comment states the consequence - 'the adapter drops every other key, so payload is unreachable by any reader, forever'. src/mica/gate4-sunset/index.ts:418,427 - leg B filters on recordKey(entry) = tupleKey([moduleId, eventType]) and compares sequenceNumber; it does not read `outcome` at all. And a1706db projects the successor paper's outcome as `tenureRef`, not `ref`, so even a reader that did read outcome would be checking the tenure binding rather than the successor reference. THE VALUE LIVES IN payload.ref AND NO READER CAN REACH IT. THE ARBITER RULED THE SHAPE on 2026-10-03 (18:37Z): shape (c) of three. (a) WIDEN THE READER - change the bridge's projection so the successor paper's outcome carries `ref`, then require it non-empty: two acts not one, the five papers stop projecting uniformly, and the outcome becomes an UNBOUNDED IDENTIFIER, which a1706db's own projection table flags as the risk that explodes a reader's class axis. (b) NARROW THE CLAIM and rely silently on the bridge: this is exactly the cross-repo dependency T22's own ground condemns - 'a core reader whose correctness rests on a regex in the bridge repo is the cross-repo dependency this project forbids, and it is not a defence src/mica can see or test'. (c) BOTH HALVES WHERE EACH BELONGS, WITH THE DEPENDENCY VERSIONED AND PRINTED. The bridge already enforces it - mica-bridge's validateSunsetRecord refuses an empty, blank or whitespace payload.ref because nonEmpty() trims, landed in a1706db four hours BEFORE Codex's FAIL on the reader arrived - and the reader gains a ceiling line naming that enforcer, that rule and THAT RELEASE, printed on every reading. 08n 3 puts successor ADEQUACY outside this principle's bound, and 04a 2 is form never truth, so the reader does not reach for content at all; non-emptiness is the thinnest edge of it. COST TODAY IS ZERO: readers.gate4Sunset is not in the live declaration (241d6db1), and gate4 is absent from the eight composing sensorIds on every decision in the book.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T24: gate 4's leg B states on every reading that the successor paper's content is enforced by the bridge, naming the bridge release it relies on, because the reader cannot see that content and must say so rather than imply a check it does not make.

conditions: 1. ONE CEILING LINE, inside the existing source-discipline fence, added to GATE4_SUNSET_CEILING_LINES so it rides every path `ceilingText` feeds. NO new check, NO new blind code, NO new finding class, NO change to either leg's logic - and this is asserted by the derivation, not promised: the suite's count moves 32 -> 35 and nothing else in the declared population moves.

2. THE LINE NAMES ALL FOUR THINGS OR IT IS SHAPE (b) WEARING SHAPE (c)'s CLOTHES: the repo that enforces it (mica-bridge), the function (validateSunsetRecord), the field and rule (payload.ref, nonEmpty() trims), and THE RELEASE (a1706db) together with the statement that a bridge OLDER than that release, or any other writer, lets an empty successor reference read SILENT here with nothing in src/mica noticing. A test asserts each of those strings is present. Without the release the line is a reassurance; with it, it is a dependency a reader can date.

3. A test asserts the line is printed on a SILENT reading, an ALARM reading AND a BLIND reading. A reader that drops its ceiling exactly when it cannot read is at its most misleading, so 'printed on every reading' is measured rather than claimed.

4. ⛔ A TEST PINS THE INDISTINGUISHABILITY THE LINE DISCLOSES: four successor values - a real brief name, "", "   ", and a tab-and-newline - produce verdicts whose summaries are IDENTICAL byte for byte, in both the leg and the composite. A disclosure nobody checks is a comment.

5. THAT TEST CARRIES THE GUARD MY FIRST PROBE LACKED, and the guard is the condition, not a courtesy: each of the four readings must be SILENT with blindReasonCodes undefined. My first measurement of this defect read CANNOT_ASSESS / [G4_READABILITY_GATE] four times because the fixture declared no readable load state - leg B never ran and I was watching the readability gate fire. FOUR IDENTICAL ROWS THAT PROVED NOTHING, and the only thing that distinguished them from the real result was printing the blind codes beside the verdict kind.

6. MUTATION EVIDENCE, two mutations and two different arms: removing the release sha from the ceiling line fails condition 2's arm and nothing else; making condition 4's fixture blind fails condition 5's guard with its own message. A check that survives a mutation of the thing it checks is not checking it.
